prose.title: Understanding murabaha
prose.intro: Murabaha is a sale at a known margin: the bank buys an asset and resells it to the client at an agreed price, payable later. Unlike an interest-bearing loan, the bank’s gain comes from a real good.
prose.p1: Three conditions are checked during a compliance audit:
prose.li1: the bank actually owns the asset before reselling it;
prose.li2: the margin is fixed in the contract and does not change;
prose.li3: no late-payment penalty benefits the bank.
prose.ol1: The client states the need and signs a promise to purchase.
prose.ol2: The bank acquires the asset from the supplier.
prose.ol3: The bank resells the asset to the client with the agreed margin.
prose.quote: Compliance is not a constraint added to the product: it is its very structure.
prose.keyPoint: Murabaha rewards a real sale, not the passage of time. If the bank never owns the asset, the transaction is not compliant.
prose.warning: This content explains general principles. It is neither a fatwa nor personalised financial advice.

faq.a1:
Between three and eight weeks depending on scope: number of products, contracts and branches.

A precise schedule is included in the proposal.

audit.title: Audit and compliance
audit.metaDescription: Sharia compliance audits of institutions, Islamic windows and financial products, based on AAOIFI standards and CEMAC regulations.
audit.lead: An independent review of your products, contracts and processes against the principles of Islamic finance and reference standards.
audit.problem1: A product presented as compliant puts the institution’s reputation on the line. Without an independent review, a gap between promise and practice can go unnoticed until a client or the regulator points it out.
audit.problem2: An audit gives management and the compliance committee a clear view of the gaps, their severity and the corrections required.
audit.ctaText: Describe your institution and the intended scope: we will come back to you with a proposal.

conseil.title: Advisory and support
conseil.metaDescription: Product structuring, Islamic windows, policies and procedures, compliance committees: step-by-step support across the CEMAC region.
conseil.lead: From product design to opening an Islamic window, we support institutions and project owners at every stage.
conseil.problem1: Demand for compliant solutions is growing, but the skills to design, document and run them remain scarce in Central Africa.
conseil.problem2: We bring a proven method, document templates and skills transfer so your teams become autonomous.
conseil.ctaText: A free, no-commitment thirty-minute call to understand your needs.

takaful.title: Takaful and finance
takaful.metaDescription: Understand takaful and Islamic financing: product design, corporate takaful, SME financing. FAQ and support.
takaful.lead: Takaful is insurance based on mutual help and risk sharing. We help insurers, companies and individuals understand and implement it.
takaful.problem1: In takaful, participants pool their contributions in a fund that belongs to them. The operator manages the fund for a transparent fee; surpluses may be redistributed.
takaful.problem2: Still little known in the CEMAC region, it meets a real demand for compliant protection. We explain how it works and support its design.
takaful.ctaText: Leave your details: an advisor will call you back to answer your questions.
